title: Chronograph render pipeline: scalable series rendering, legend semantics & tooltip accessibility
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Our time-series component is struggling with large datasets (hundreds to thousands of series) and complex interaction states. Current issues observed: slow initial render, janky hover/tooltip responses, large DOM for legends causing layout thrash, and tooltip content is not reliably exposed to screen readers.

Goal:
Redesign the rendering pipeline and surface affordances so charts remain responsive at scale and are accessible. Deliver a design spec + interaction pattern that engineers can implement with batching/decimation strategies, a small DOM legend mode, and accessible tooltip semantics. Ensure color/token guidance for high-contrast and color-blind palettes and clear keyboard flows.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Include both canvas and SVG fallbacks; prefer canvas for heavy-series renders.
- Do not redesign chart API; this is purely component-level UX and accessibility work.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Rendering pipeline: progressive micro-batching render strategy that shows coarse decimated overview quickly (LTTB or simple downsample) then refines in subsequent frames. Use requestAnimationFrame + web-worker decimation for heavy datasets. Provide a documented "render-mode" token (fast | balanced | precise) in design doc.
2) Legend semantics: introduce a compact legend mode (virtualized list with keyboard pagination) and a grouped mode for series families. Preserve semantic reading order: group label -> toggle control -> color swatch -> series label -> metadata chip. Ensure focusable elements have visible focus tokens.
3) Tooltips: make tooltip content available to assistive tech via aria-describedby + offscreen live summary when hovered/focused; provide keyboard hover equivalence (focus on point reveals tooltip). Support a persistent detail panel mode for touch.
4) Accessibility: explicit rules for aria roles (role="application" only if necessary), aria-live usage limited to summary changes, reduced-motion respect, high-contrast token variants, and clear instructions for screen reader authors.
5) Performance UX: loading skeleton for chart area, skeleton legend while series metadata resolves, progressive reveal to avoid blank screens. Document thresholds where canvas should be default (e.g., > 250 series or > 10k points total).

Acceptance criteria (design):
- Annotated Figma screens for 3 dataset sizes: small (<=10 series), medium (10-250), large (>250).
- Interaction spec for keyboard navigation: tab order, arrow key series focus, legend toggle via space/enter.
- Tooltip accessibility pattern with ARIA attributes and a fallback live summary.
- A 1-page dev handoff with guidance on tokens (focus, hover, high-contrast), recommended decimation algorithm options, and visual specs for compact legend.

Engineering handoff notes (for implementation):
- Provide recommended defaults: render-mode=balanced, decimation=adaptive-LTTB, canvasFallbackThreshold=250.
- Legend virtualization: provide height/row metrics and focusable container role="listbox" pattern.
- Tooltip: ensure content has an id and chart elements have aria-describedby referencing that id; expose a separate aria-live region for summarised metric changes for screen reader consumption.

Design tasks:
- Create Figma frames for the 3 dataset tiers and the compact legend component (Ava).
- Define color token variants and accessible palettes (Mateo + Accessibility consultant).
- Draft interaction flow for keyboard-first users (Ava).

Dependencies:
- Needs ENG-5028 (chart runtime decimation helpers) and ENG-5099 (legend virtualization API).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Canvas gives performance, but loses native DOM semantics — mitigated by exposing aria attributes on a parallel invisible DOM layer for accessibility.
- Progressive refinement may cause visual "popping" as details load; will provide skeletons and subtle crossfade tokens to reduce perceived jank.

Deliverables:
- Figma file with annotated specs and tokens (link in Links).
- Design handoff doc + minimal interaction prototypes.
- Accessibility checklist and QA test cases.

QA / acceptance testing points:
- Keyboard-only navigation across legend and chart points (no mouse).
- Screen reader reads meaningful summary on focus/tooltip reveal.
- Performance smoke: initial render < 500ms for medium datasets (10-250 series) on target test machine.

Notes for follow-up:
- After initial implementation, run user testing with a screen reader user and with a product team dashboard containing >500 series for telemetry.
